phase3_findings.summary: Step 1 no longer independently enforces the four always-on reviewers; it now trusts the engine's self-reported expected_reviewers (guarded only for non-emptiness). A correlated engine bug that under-fans Phase 3 and reports a matching under-fanned roster (dropping an always-on for a non-first-only reason) would pass Step 1 vacuously; the sole remaining detector is the Step 2.6 shadow's always-on floor.
phase3_findings.disposition: acknowledged-deliberate-tradeoff: only the engine can evaluate pr-test-analyzer's test-relevance predicate and the first-only iter>=2 drop, which is why the operand moved to the engine-reported roster; the always-on floor is retained at the independent shadow re-review. Not a REJECT.

phase3_findings.summary: The shadow's malformed-shape wording relies on 'an empty or sub-floor reported roster is a coverage shortfall' rather than Step 1's explicit 'present and a non-empty array'. A wrong-type (non-array) expected_reviewers is still handled fail-closed (sub-floor -> outcome 3) but the reasoning is implicit; mirroring Step 1's phrasing would improve clarity.
phase3_findings.disposition: clarity-only suggestion; failure direction already closed. Not blocking.

report: APPROVE. PR #1927 (issue #1904) rewires the fix loop's Step-1 and shadow reviewer-roster well-formedness check to compare the dispatched roster against a new engine-reported `expected_reviewers` return member (the engine's own Phase 3.1 gate decisions) instead of recomputing the expected roster from `diff_profile`, which cannot express pr-test-analyzer's test-relevance predicate. All seven acceptance criteria are satisfied: (AC1) neither loop-control.md nor shadow-review.md derives pr-test-analyzer's membership from diff_profile alone; (AC2) both name `expected_reviewers` as the evaluable operand; (AC3) the two loop-control.md paragraphs now agree that presence cannot be cross-checked against diff_profile; (AC4) the fallback-to-inline protection is preserved and strengthened — a died subagent, an out-of-set dispatch_mode, a missing/unreadable/short return file, and now a non-present/empty/wrong-type expected_reviewers all fall back to inline, closing the vacuity hole; (AC5) all four carriers (loop-control.md, shadow-review.md, and both SKILL.md schema examples at top-level line 109 and shadow-block line 251) show the same member name and identifier vocabulary; (AC6) expected_reviewers was added to ITER_EXPECTED_FIELDS as an unconditional field and NOT to the synth set, LR_CONDITIONAL_FIELDS is unchanged so the single-source divergence guard stays green, and a new consumer assertion verifies --self-check warns on its omission; (AC7) a changeset is present. The two internal docs (DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md by-path field list + roster line, shadow-review.md 'expected roster is mechanical' bullet) are reconciled — confirming the iter-3 Important finding is fixed. loop-control.md now constrains expected_reviewers to 'present and a non-empty array' (iter-3 Suggestion fixed). The shipped consumer bodies name no repo-private path or issue number. Fail-closed behavior on the merge-gating path is preserved; the always-on floor remains enforced at the independent shadow. Two non-blocking findings: one Minor documenting the deliberate reduction of the parent's independent always-on floor at Step 1 (an intrinsic consequence of moving to the engine-reported operand, backstopped by the shadow), and one Suggestion to make the shadow's wrong-type handling wording as explicit as Step 1's. Neither warrants REJECT.
